answer: A beacon burns only while watched, so standing must be re-earned each epoch. Each identity needs two holders outside its own wharf to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one crew. Every voyage is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. An audit replays a random claim each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond, which cannot be pooled or resold.
